reviews.summary: Right now the lead is a framing plus a table of contents. Someone who searched for reveal ideas should get two real ones before they scroll.; This is backwards. Their reaction appears on your screen, and asking them to record would tip them off. A reader following it as written would miss the moment.; The schema caps each clue at 40 characters (src/templates/pack-your-bags/schema.ts). Lines like "Three nights. Bring enough for four, just in case." are longer, so anyone pasting them in would hit the limit.; A scavenger or treasure hunt is one of the most common reveal ideas on the current top results, and the post doesn't have it. Add it as its own list item after the decoy present.; The tip

Each clue is capped at 40 characters (schema.ts clues .max(40)) and is shown as an item to pack ('Pack {thing}'), so the table's example lines don't fit: "Three nights. Bring enough for four, just in case." is 51 characters and "One nice dinner. Everything else is walking." is 44. The nights already appear on the date tag (Pack.tsx DateTag).; Same 40-character limit. Also, next to the imperative 'usa', «Mete» reads as an instruction to the reader, when it's the recipient who packs. The English says 'They pack'.; A missing visa or ESTA/ETA is the classic way a secret trip falls apart, and a top result on this topic would cover it. A scavenger hunt around the house is in nearly every top result for 'surprise trip reveal ideas' (getawaytoday, lostontheroute, AAA, Disney reveal posts); the post's week of clues is by text, so the in-person hunt is missing.; The table and the description promise 'at the door or the airport', but no section gives a reveal for that timing; top results (getawaytoday, AAA, travel guides) all cover disguising departure day as an ordinary errand.; With the cover-story item the section covers the 'at the door / airport' row of the table, and the heading should say so, so every timing in the description has a matching heading.

reviews.summary: 'Passport details' undersells both forms. The ESTA asks for their address, employer and parents' names plus eligibility questions, and the UK ETA asks for a photo of their face. Someone planning to do it in secret should know that before they book.; The same fix in Spanish.; Once you share your screen in FaceTime, WhatsApp or Zoom, the other person shrinks to a small tile or disappears, so a screen recording made while sharing mostly shows the booking page, not their reaction.; The same fix in Spanish.; Without the reflexive, «resérvalas» next to a trip reads as 'book them'. «Resérvatelas» is how you'd say 'keep them free' in Spain.

applied: ESTA/ETA: the forms need personal details and (ETA) a face photo, so you may need their help; allow a few days (EN+ES)
Video call: hold up the ticket or the booking on a second device so their face stays full size, record before showing (EN+ES)
